title: Killed for memory
story: relax_all.sh keeps dying a few minutes in. Submit it, work out what went wrong, fix it, and get a run that completes.

lesson.title: How --mem works

parts.note: The most RAM the whole job may use, here 48 GB. `M` means megabytes.

lesson.why: Memory is shared too. Slurm kills a job that uses more than it asked for, so it can't crowd out other jobs.
lesson.without: Too little and `sacct` shows OUT_OF_MEMORY. `seff JOBID` shows how much the job actually used, so you know what to ask for.

files.~/{{project}}/relax_all.sh:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=relax
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --output=slurm-%j.out

module load rosetta
for f in designs/*.pdb; do relax.linuxgccrelease -s $f; done
